agent_notes: The Hebrew verse is the superscription, which the KJV leaves unnumbered (61:0) and runs into its 'A Psalm of David'. The Hebrew has no word for 'psalm' (mizmor); the KJV and ASV supply it. I kept it out of the literal layer and marked it in brackets only in the dramatic layer.

negînat: the vowel is pointed as a construct (patach) but the form is read as a plain singular of neginah (Ibn Ezra, Radak, Meiri). The 'stringed instrument' sense follows Metzudat Zion and the versions; 'melody' or 'song' is equally possible, and the Targum takes it as 'praises'. I glossed it 'stringed music' to keep both.

Revised after the reviewer request: the literal layer says 'wrapped [in faintness]' and the note on בַּעֲטֹף no longer says 'darkness'. 'Faintness' rests on the Targum (אִשְׁתַּלְהֲיוּת) and on Metzudat Zion's 'wrapping, clothing'; Radak instead reads the wrapping as the heaping up of prayer in distress. I follow the first reading.

STEPBible glosses בְּצוּר יָרוּם מִמֶּנִּי as 'on a rock [which] it is high more than me'. I keep the ב as 'on/to' and take מִמֶּנִּי as comparative, 'too high for me', as the five English versions all do. The sense is a rock beyond my own reach, which only God can set me on.

The note on דֹּר וָדֹר now says Rashi's seventy is the total.
